1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.g3 Nf6 4.Bg2 Be7 5.O-.strategy: Castles first and keeps a central advance and a second fianchetto in reserve. White waits to see how Black sets up and commits to a plan only then.
1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.g3 Nf6 4.Bg2 Be7 5.O-.name: English Opening: Agincourt Defence, Neo-Catalan Declined

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.g3 Nf6 4.Bg2 Be7 5.d4.strategy: Occupies the centre with a pawn and sets the c4-d4 pair against Black's d5-e6 structure. White plays for a small, lasting space advantage and queenside pressure; in return the c4-pawn can become a target if Black takes it.
1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.g3 Nf6 4.Bg2 Be7 5.d4.name: Catalan Opening: Closed
1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.g3 Nf6 4.Bg2 Be7 5.d4.background: The Catalan is named for Catalonia: the organisers of the Barcelona tournament of 1929 asked Savielly Tartakower to create a new variation in homage to Catalonia's chess history.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.g3 Nf6 4.Bg2 Be7 5.b3.strategy: Chooses the double fianchetto: both bishops will aim at the centre and the queenside from a distance, and the c4-pawn is firmly protected. The central pawn advance is postponed, so Black gets time to claim a share of the centre.
1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.g3 Nf6 4.Bg2 Be7 5.b3.name: English Opening: Agincourt Defence, Neo-Catalan Declined, Early b3

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.g3 Nf6 4.Bg2 Be7 5.b3.strategy: Mirrors White's set-up: the queen's bishop goes to the long diagonal to fight for the centre, and both sides now play with a double fianchetto. Black frees the c8-bishop from behind the e6-pawn but still has no central pawn break.
1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.g3 Nf6 4.Bg2 Be7 5.b3.name: English Opening: Agincourt Defence, Neo-Catalan Declined, Early b3

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.g3 Nf6 4.Bg2 Be7 5.b3.strategy: Challenges the centre instead of copying White's set-up, and takes d4 away from the pieces White is preparing. Black accepts an open game, in which the d5-pawn loses one of its pawn defenders if White takes on d5.
1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.g3 Nf6 4.Bg2 Be7 5.b3.name: English Opening: Agincourt Defence, Neo-Catalan Declined, Early b3

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.g3 Nf6 4.Bg2 Be7 5.d4.strategy: Gets the king to safety before the tension in the centre is resolved, and keeps the sturdy d5-e6 pawn chain. Black leaves the fight for the centre until White shows what the queenside pressure will look like.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.g3 Nf6 4.Bg2 Be7 5.O-.strategy: Finishes the kingside development and gets the king safe before Black commits in the centre. The compact structure stays intact and Black waits for White to show a plan, with the c8-bishop still the shut-in piece.
Challenges the centre before castling: the c-pawn hits d4, and the exchange on d5 would open lines for Black's pieces. Black seeks active counterplay and accepts a small delay in castling.
